# Infoscend - Commercial Intelligence Platform

> Infoscend is the commercial intelligence platform for companies that distribute through third-party networks. It manages every route to market - general trade, modern trade, and e-commerce - as channels of one consented commercial truth, on one database with one reasoning engine. Tagline: Strategy flows down. Intelligence flows up. The loop closes.

## Brand

- Name: Infoscend (pronounced in-fo-send)
- Etymology: info + scend (the upward lift of a wave; information ascending)
- Tagline: Strategy flows down. Intelligence flows up. The loop closes.
- Positioning line: the distributor owns the data, the brand earns the view, the loop closes.
- Voice: practitioner-direct, numbers-first, no marketing softeners

## What Infoscend stands for (four convictions, enforced in the data model)

1. Every channel as one - general trade, modern trade, and e-commerce are managed together on one consented sell-out spine that records what sold, at what net price, funded by whom. Total sell-out and cross-channel cannibalisation in one view. This is the keystone.
2. Distributor-first data sovereignty - the distributor owns all operational data; a brand is a tag and sees only its own slice, and only through consent that can be withdrawn. No monolithic shared tenant.
3. AI as actor, not advisor - every AI output is a constraint-validated draft on a real entity, launched by one human click. Accept, amend, or discard. Nothing executes without a human.
4. One reasoning engine - detect, diagnose across lenses, prescribe by cause, human accept/amend/discard, then learn. Every AI surface is a face of the same engine, and it improves with use.

## Core capabilities (one platform, one database, one engine)

- Distribution Management (DMS): multi-principal, distributor-first operational backbone. Primary and multi-brand secondary orders, billing, inventory with weighted-average cost, credit control, batch tracking, multi-warehouse, distributor and outlet 360. Every read scoped through consent.
- Sales Force Automation (SFA): mobile-first field app for distributor reps. Engine-driven next-best-action before each outlet call, GPS-verified visits, vision product recognition, voice journaling, offline-first, one-thumb capture, multilingual.
- Competitive Intelligence: reps photograph competitor shelves and price lists; the engine recognises products, extracts prices, flags anomalies, and maintains a price-aspiration matrix.
- Trade Marketing, Schemes & Claims: build promotions from familiar mechanics that compile to composable contracts; run them, claim against them, and settle fast through one money path; trade-spend governance.
- Channels (modern trade & e-commerce): the same sell-out spine extended to banners and marketplaces; total-market view, true margin net of platform fees, cross-channel cannibalisation, price-corridor and grey-market alerts.
- Maju retailer loyalty: a retailer app for warung and kedai owners; multi-brand loyalty, QR scan-to-earn, reward catalogue, a direct brand-to-outlet line that routes back into orders; phone-OTP, no portal.

## Enterprise trust (day one)

- Consent-gated: no read crosses a party line without consent; a bare query that trusts the client is treated as a defect.
- Cross-tenant isolation tested, not assumed; the brand wall holds on reads and writes; tests go red when a protection is removed.
- Fail-closed: development bypasses are impossible in production; a verification gate (typecheck, isolation, money math, security) must pass before anything ships.
- Money is exact-precision with a currency companion, through a single settlement path with worked examples and golden tests.
- The bar for every change: would it pass a penetration test and security review with no comments?

## The learning loop (the compounding moat)

- Learns at the organisation level from what you accept, amend, and discard; amendments are the strongest signal.
- Provider-agnostic and self-hostable - the learning lives in your substrate, not a vendor's.
- Field response closes the loop: what the outlet did next tunes the next recommendation.

## Target market

FMCG, lubricants and fuel retail, automotive aftermarket, industrial and chemicals, pharma distribution, consumer durables - any company distributing through third-party networks. Typical buyer: Founder/GM, Head of Sales, Head of Brand, or Commercial Director.
